memoryClasses.description: Who the user is professionally: role, firm context, recurring professional identity facts.
prohibitedUses: treating profile facts as client facts
using profile facts as legal authority

memoryClasses.description: How the user wants TINA to respond: style, format, language of analysis.
allowedUses: tone and format selection within approved formats
examples: wants strict continuity in TINA development

memoryClasses.description: Facts and state of one specific engagement, case, or workstream.
allowedUses: answer continuity within the same matter
prohibitedUses: use in unrelated matters or clients

memoryClasses.description: Facts about one specific client or entity.
allowedUses: entity type and registration context within the client scope

memoryClasses.description: Facts supplied during one conversation, not yet approved for storage.
allowedUses: contextual continuity within the active session only
prohibitedUses: persistence beyond the session without consent
examples: facts not yet approved for storage

memoryClasses.description: Facts about TINA's own indexed sources: metadata, availability, provenance notes. Always defers to live index state and sourceAvailability classification at answer time.
Content that must never be stored, or only with explicit logged consent where legally necessary.
prohibitedUses: any echo of secret values into logs or events
examples: health/personal data unless explicitly necessary and consented

permissionLevels.description: Item must not be written at all.
permissionLevels.allowedUse: use in the current response only
permissionLevels.prohibitedUse: any persistence or log echo of the value
permissionLevels.example: an API key pasted by mistake

permissionLevels.description: Kept only for the active conversation.
permissionLevels.example: assume 8% income tax option for this computation

permissionLevels.prohibitedUse: use in other matters/clients or as general law

permissionLevels.retentionConcept: until client relationship ended or erased
permissionLevels.prohibitedUse: cross-client use or generalization into tax law

permissionLevels.description: Attached to the user's own profile.
permissionLevels.prohibitedUse: treating preferences as facts about clients
permissionLevels.example: user is a CPA and prefers concise memos

permissionLevels.prohibitedUse: storing user or client personal data under this label

permissionLevels.description: May be stored only after an affirmative user approval recorded with the item; composes with a scope.
permissionLevels.allowedUse: as approved by the recorded consent event
permissionLevels.prohibitedUse: storage without a logged consent event

confidenceStates.description: Stated or approved explicitly by the user.
Deduced by TINA; must be labeled; never sufficient alone to skip a clarification question.
From TINA's own index metadata; defers to live index state.
Past its freshness horizon; usable only with re-confirmation.
Conflicts with newer input; excluded from answers until resolved.
Supplied by a third channel and not yet confirmed; treated like inferred.

the BIR LOA matter for taxable year 2023

scopeTypes.description: Metadata bound to an indexed source.
scopeTypes.example: provenance note for an indexed RMC document

prohibitedMemoryRules.description: API keys must never be stored.
Private credentials and secrets must never be stored.
Unsupported legal conclusions must never be stored as memory.
Unsupported tax conclusions must never be stored as memory.
Unsupported accusations must never be stored.
Raw confidential file contents must not be stored without explicit storage approval.
Sensitive personal data must not be stored unless explicitly necessary to the service and consented.
Court case currentness claims must not be stored or asserted; Phase 10 legal-state validation is deferred.
G.R. case-name lookup conclusions must not be stored or asserted before Phase 10.
Source supersession or currentness claims must not be stored or asserted before Phase 10.
Facts from one client must not be assumed for another client.
Matter facts must never be used or stored as general tax law.

authoritySafetyRules.description: Memory is inserted as context constraints, never as authority.
Memory has zero influence on sourceAvailability/SAE classification.
Memory must not alter retrieval behavior or results.
Memory never adds, removes, reorders, or rewords source cards (Authority Lock).
Memory must not bypass or override authority gates.
Memory must never produce or support fabricated citations.
Memory must not assert legal currentness, supersession, or case status.
Memory must not substitute for sourceAvailability classification or source-grounded answers.
Facts stated in the live conversation always outrank stored memory.
Conflicting stored memory is marked contradicted and triggers clarification, never silent override.

consentRules.description: An explicit user save command allows storage with a one-sentence scope confirmation.
Sensitive or confidential client facts require explicit consent before durable storage.
Matter facts require scope confirmation (matter vs session-only) once per matter session.
Inferred items must be confirmed by the user before any durable write.
User corrections update stored memory with old-vs-new shown and scope preserved.
A forget/delete request must be honored immediately, confirmed, and logged.
Facts from confidential documents are never stored automatically.
Every durable write must carry exactly one permission level; unlabeled writes are rejected.

deferredBoundaries.description: PATCH-07B-CLARIFICATION-BOUNDARY-TUNING-1 remains a Phase 7B pre-production-ON follow-up, not Phase 8 memory work.
Official source repository governance, source freshness, and legal-state validation are Phase 10.
Court case metadata registry, G.R. number lookup, jurisprudence applicability/currentness/supersession are Phase 10.
Hallucination trap evaluation and HAL-TEST.xlsx items are Phase 10.
Observability, query evidence logging, tracing, cache headers, compression, CDN/static caching, API response caching, vector/search performance are Phase 11.
Document-aware advisory, uploaded client document intelligence, working-paper extraction are Phase 12.
Mobile app comes after Phase 13 only.
